thread.title: Reps. Tenney and Correa named co-chairs of Congressional Family Business Caucus
thread.title_full: Reps. Tenney and Correa named co-chairs of Congressional Family Business Caucus

author: j. s. hightower
title: Reps. Tenney and Correa named co-chairs of Congressional Family Business Caucus
text:
Congresswoman Claudia Tenney and Congressman Lou Correa have been named co-chairs of the bipartisan Congressional Family Business Caucus for the 119th Congress, according to a March 11 announcement. The caucus will hold its first meeting of the year on March 17 at the U.S. Capitol Visitor Center, bringing together lawmakers, family business leaders, and policy experts to discuss issues facing family-owned businesses.
The caucus was created to educate members of Congress about the role that family-owned businesses play in the American economy. According to research cited by organizers, there are more than 32 million family-owned businesses in the United States, supporting over 83 million jobs and contributing $7.7 trillion annually to gross domestic product—nearly 59 percent of the private workforce.
The upcoming meeting will focus on “Pricing and Profits: Affordability Strategies for Family-Owned Businesses” and will include presentations from business owners, policy experts, and representatives from Family Enterprise USA. The event is organized by Family Enterprise USA and Family Enterprise USA Action.
“Family-owned businesses are the backbone of communities across the country, creating jobs, supporting local economies, and carrying on traditions that span generations. As someone who helped run my family’s business, I understand the unique challenges these businesses face, from rising costs and workforce pressures to complex regulations and tax policy. I look forward to working with Congressman Correa and our colleagues in the Caucus to ensure family businesses have a strong voice in Congress and the policies they need to grow, compete, and continue supporting millions of American workers,” said Congresswoman Tenney.
“Our economy is driven by family businesses whose owners and employees are usually our neighbors. My parents worked hard to give me the opportunity to reach the middle class, and starting a family business provides the same possibility to millions of Americans,” Rep. Correa said. “We need to make sure that family businesses continue to flourish across different industries, and the Family Business Caucus will work to help Main Street entrepreneurs achieve their American Dream.”
Pat Soldano, President of Family Enterprise USA, said: “We’re grateful to see Representatives Tenney and Correa co-chair the Congressional Family Business Caucus for the 119th Congress. We’re also excited to kick-off this year’s meetings with the theme of affordability strategies for family businesses. Our two co-chairs are intimately familiar with the struggles and unique challenges family-owned businesses face versus traditional corporations. We look forward to their leadership in helping family-owned businesses get their voices heard in Congress.”
Tenney has represented New York’s 24th district since replacing Anthony Brindisi in 2021 [according to available records]. She previously served in the New York State Assembly from 2011 through 2016 [according to legislative history]. Born in New Hartford in 1961, Tenney currently lives in Canandaigua [according to biographical information]. She graduated from Colgate University with a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1983 before earning her law degree from University of Cincinnati in 1987 [according to educational records].
